name: telnet_loopback
description: telnetd P2: /testbin/telnetd backgrounded on 127.0.0.1:2323 with telnet(1) connecting to it in the same emulator -- no hardware, no host, no second machine.  PROVEN: bind+listen on a loopback address, connect() matching the listener, accept() pairing the descriptors, the pty opening, spawnx() of /bin/getty, and a clean client session.  NOT asserted: the 'login:' prompt.  It DOES render -- the full chain was observed reaching 'FGX/gs / login:' -- but ONLY when the client carries an extra stdout write (a debug printf) between telrcv() and ttyflush().  Without it the 15 bytes reach the tty buffer (TTYBYTES()=15, SYNCHing=0, flushout=0) and ttyflush() is entered, yet nothing appears, and a 90s timeout does not help -- so it is not timing.  Asserting 'login:' here would make the gate depend on a heisenbug, so it asserts the three facts that hold unconditionally.
